clue.text: Kid getting into music roots out old footwear

indicators.note: getting into says the leather word goes inside the music word

parts.note: the blues is a musical genre
kid is soft goatskin leather, close kin to suede
to hoe is to dig or root out weeds

explanation.surface: Roots music fans dig out a pair of old shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' reads as a child but is the leather; 'getting into' signals the container. The answer is also the 1950s rock-and-roll song, setting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoes made of napped leather are footwear, and the style is associated with the 1950s.

clue.text: Could be Lulworth skipper having abandoned heading misses France completely

indicators.note: misses means a letter is left out of what remains
abandoning its heading means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: the Lulworth skipper is a species of butterfly found in Dorset
F is the international abbreviation for France

explanation.surface: A Dorset butterfly loses its way and fails to reach France.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lulworth skipper is a small British butterfly named after Lulworth Cove in Dorset; drop its first letter B and then the F.
explanation.definitionFit: Utterly is an adverb of totality, synonymous with entirely.

clue.text: Wise ignoring half of sausages' ingredients

indicators.note: ignoring the first half of the word leaves only its back end to read from
ingredients points to letters contained inside the word

explanation.surface: A cook makes sausages but skips half the recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: The herb is itself a classic sausage ingredient, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sage is a wise person, and as an adjective the word means wise or judicious.

clue.text: Waste burger one tucked into with energy before

indicators.note: before places the energy letter at the front of the rest

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
a Big Mac is a well-known burger
I is the Roman numeral one
to tuck into food is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: Someone wolfs down a burger with plenty of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To emaciate is to make thin and wasted, so waste as a verb fits.

clue.text: Hazel perhaps will follow two directions in course

indicators.note: will follow puts the tree after the compass points

parts.note: E and N are east and north
hazel is an example of a tree

explanation.surface: Someone called Hazel is given directions to a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazel' looks like a woman's name but is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is a course of a meal, the main dish in American usage.

clue.text: Hospital may hope to offset treatment

indicators.note: offset suggests the letters are knocked out of position and rearranged

explanation.surface: A hospital hopes alternative therapy can balance things out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offset' rearranges MAY HOPE TO into OMEOPATHY after H.
explanation.definitionFit: Homeopathy is a form of alternative medical therapy.

clue.text: Take the edge off delightful impression

indicators.note: taking off the edge means dropping the letter at the front

parts.note: fetching means attractive or delightful

explanation.surface: Advice on softening a pleasant first impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take the edge off' strips the leading F from FETCHING.
explanation.definitionFit: An etching is a print, an impression taken from an etched plate.

clue.text: Come a cropper cutting into opening question

indicators.note: cutting means one piece slices into the middle of another

parts.note: taken as written
to come a cropper is to fail or blunder, so err
a gate is an opening in a wall or fence

explanation.surface: A rider falls badly through an open gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come a cropper' is British slang for having a fall or failure.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrogate is to question closely.

clue.text: Gatsby recalled except via a name in books still?

indicators.note: recalled reads the trimmed name backwards
except means the following word is taken away

parts.note: by means via, by way of

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the books abbreviation

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A reader recalls The Great Gatsby and wonders about names in books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except' removes the word for 'via' and 'recalled' turns what is left round, giving the deer; 'in' signals the container. Gatsby is the F. Scott Fitzgerald character.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water is still and not flowing, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Fellow embraces company and wine

indicators.note: embraces means the man word wraps around the company abbreviation

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man hugs his colleagues over a bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Macon is a French Burgundy wine from around the town of the same name.

clue.text: Austin maybe left benefits protecting popular originator of 1

parts.note: Austin is a British car make

indicators.note: protecting means the benefits word wraps around the popular word

parts.note: perks are benefits of a job
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A car with benefits is supposedly popular with rock pioneers.
explanation.walkthrough: Austin was a British car manufacturer. The answer wrote and first recorded the song at 1-across.
explanation.definitionFit: This rockabilly singer composed and first recorded the shoe song in 1955.

clue.text: Hairstyle making a comeback in 'Doctor Faustus'

indicators.note: making a comeback says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters are found inside the play's title

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A revival of Marlowe's play features a retro hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded, bushy hairstyle.

clue.text: Tip off, using good English, about arranged eviction

indicators.note: about means the two letters go around the rearranged word
arranged means the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A landlord warns a tenant about a planned eviction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' reshuffles the fodder into IVENOTIC, and 'about' wraps the good and English letters round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To tip someone off is to warn them, and giving notice is a formal warning.

clue.text: Overdue, Sun taking blame sadly for Jerry Lee Lewis and 11 among others

definitions.text: Jerry Lee Lewis and 11 among others

indicators.note: taking means the overdue word holds the rearranged letters

parts.note: late means overdue

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters are disturbed and reshuffled

explanation.surface: A late payment to Sun Records gets blamed on a rock star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' reshuffles the fodder into BELMA and 'taking' puts it inside. Sun Records in Memphis signed both musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists on the same record label are colleagues of that kind, as these were at Sun.

clue.text: Desolate amateur shrink

parts.note: lay means non-professional, amateur
to waste is to shrink or dwindle

explanation.surface: A desolate amateur goes to see a psychiatrist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrink' looks like a psychiatrist but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To desolate a place is to devastate it, which is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Garden rubbish hazard

indicators.note: rubbish suggests the letters are trashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Garden waste poses a hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: A danger is a hazard or risk.

clue.text: Being on strike for an aid to survival

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: being means existence or life
to belt is to strike hard

explanation.surface: A living worker on strike needs help to survive.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifebelt is a buoyant ring thrown to keep someone afloat.

clue.text: Same two chords in Emerson Lake and Palmer's records

indicators.note: in means the chord letters sit inside the band's initials

parts.note: ELP is the prog rock band Emerson, Lake and Palmer; the possessive gives S
E and E are two identical musical notes or chords

explanation.surface: A prog band's albums use the same two chords over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: An elpee is a phonetic spelling of LP, a long-playing record.

clue.text: Auntie P rarely reveals her name

indicators.note: rarely suggests something unusual done to the letters, a reordering

explanation.surface: An aunt known by an initial seldom tells anyone her name.
explanation.walkthrough: AUNTIE P rearranges to the name of a flower; Petunia is also Harry Potter's aunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Petunia is a girl's name, taken from the garden flower.

clue.text: Visual humour landmark requires silence

parts.note: a sight is a notable landmark worth seeing
to gag is to silence

explanation.surface: A famous landmark demands that visitors keep quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight gag is a joke that works through what is seen rather than said.

clue.text: Cook — no learner — set grill for rubbery piece of meat

indicators.note: cook means the letters are worked over into a new form
no means the learner letter is excluded

parts.note: L is the learner driver plate letter

explanation.surface: A cook with no trainee sets the grill and produces tough meat.
explanation.walkthrough: SET GRILL without an L rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gristle is tough cartilage in meat that is chewy and rubbery.

clue.text: Making an effort can be distressing

definitions.meaning: upsetting or annoying, as in a tiresome day

explanation.definitionFit: Trying means attempting and also describes something hard to bear.

clue.text: Bird of prey noticed displaying evidence of conformity

parts.note: a kite is a bird of prey
marked means noticed or observed

explanation.surface: A bird of prey was spotted showing off.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kitemark is the British Standards Institution's safety and quality certification mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A product bearing the Kitemark has been certified as meeting a British standard.

clue.text: Marrow in haggis? Turnips apparently

indicators.note: in signals letters lying inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Scot asks whether the haggis contains marrow, or is it just turnips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marrow' suggests the vegetable, but means the core or essence.
explanation.definitionFit: The marrow of a matter is its essence, the central point.

clue.text: Boss's doubt is not even raised

definitions.note: the possessive stands for 'Boss is', so the noun boss alone is the definition and the 's is a link meaning is

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters are read upwards
not even means keep the odd-numbered letters

explanation.surface: A boss's doubt is never raised evenly.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of DOUBT IS give DUTS, turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a raised ornamental knob, as is a boss.

clue.text: High wire safety issue making work for nine

definitions.meaning: a tightrope act without any safety mesh beneath it, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a musical piece written for nine players or voices.

clue.text: One with depression, needing vermouth — unknown brand

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a dent is a small depression
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Someone depressed needs a vermouth from an unfamiliar brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin and It' is a British cocktail of gin and Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporate identity is the distinctive image of a company, its brand.

clue.text: Head latterly went on about sense and shrewdness of judgment

indicators.note: latterly means this piece comes at the end
about means the travelling word goes around the sense word

parts.note: fared means got on or went on
sight is one of the five senses
a ness is a headland, a head

explanation.surface: A head teacher went on about sense and good judgment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' is a headland, NESS, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresight in planning is good judgment about future events.
